Two weeks. That's it.
Fourteen days until Election Day, and I don't plan to spend a single one of them sitting back and hoping for the best.

| | | We said opponents of voting rights are getting desperate, Team.

**New, leaked audio has come out of Michigan** , where 14-year Congressman Mike Rogers is running again for U.S. Senate. He lost to Elissa Slotkin in 2024 and is the Republican Party's nominee again this fall against Abdul El-Sayed.

With Trump, our small farms and ranchers have faced skyrocketing costs, roller-coaster tariffs, and markets flooded with foreign goods — all direct consequences of Trump’s actions. That’s not right. Our farmers deserve better, and I’m doing something about it. | [SUPPORT SMALL FARMERS ✍️](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141843992/654921280/-1366721668?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261020_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OTc0ZGE2Zi1lM2NjLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=53_bB-rm_1ycftiqdI_NNfalNG0wyL1Kll-Kv1NNKzs=&emci=82b4a169-e3cc-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=9974da6f-e3cc-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=252045)

Without our bill, small farms often face bigger barriers to accessing funding.
_**That’s not fair.**_
Our legislation would make it easier for small farms and ranches to access USDA conservation funding and give them more support to invest in practices that protect their land, soil, and water.
**Small farmers nationwide are doing the hard work of feeding our communities and caring for our land. They deserve a government that works for them, too.**

name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.
Hey folks, it’s Mark Kelly.
Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.
I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.
So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.
I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.
I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.
After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.
**[I’m asking you to split a donation between Chris Pappas and me. We’re going to do everything we can to take back Congress this November, and Chris Pappas needs your help. I just hope you know that I wouldn’t be asking if this wasn’t important.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261020_4.V0ct8D&refcode=em20261020-4&t=1&akid=9653%2E582294%2EPoKsp4)**

Thank you.

And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too. I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help. I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance. After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do. Thank you. Mark

build: One that answers to voters. Or one that answers only to Donald
Trump.

But Derek, we can’t
be naive. Good ideas — hell, even a good, long record of results — can’t
win elections on their own. We need folks to hear about that record, and
that takes an enormous amount of resources.

Campaign literature, organizers, TV ads, rallies, gas for the campaign bus
— all of it is necessary to run a winning campaign in the most competitive
battleground state in the country.

But if we don’t get our budget in order before midnight tonight? Every
single arm of our campaign could be dealing with cuts at this time
tomorrow.

Peter, I
wish I didn't have to constantly be fundraising.

I'd rather spend every hour in union halls and town halls than write
emails like this one. But you deserve an honest answer about why I keep
asking, so here it is.

It all goes back to the disastrous Citizens United decision, which
unleashed dark money spending into our democratic process.

When one super PAC can spend $30 million trying to annihilate the
character of a candidate, that alone tells you what's wrong with Citizens
United. It's anti-democratic on its own terms.

We’re facing even more than that — over $100,000,000. And all of it is
coming from Trump’s donor network, Elon Musk, AIPAC, and countless other
outside spenders who would greatly benefit from sending a corporate hack
(Mike Rogers) to the U.S. Senate.

You have to raise excessive amounts of cash just to stay competitive in a
statewide race like ours. Some candidates take corporate checks to fund
their campaigns in exchange for their loyalty. I refuse to do that.

Our campaign has taken zero dollars from corporate PACs or AIPAC, and
we’re not about to start doing so with 14 days to go.

The only way we compete in this broken system, win, and then change it is
if we dig deep together.

When we win, I'm going to the Senate to overturn Citizens United, ban
outside spending through super PACs, and move to public funding of
elections. But first, we have to get through this fight.

It’s the many versus the money. We can win this, but only if we all show
up.

Friend,
Can you believe it? We’re officially 14 days away from Election Day! Before I share why these next two weeks are hands down the most important and consequential of the campaign, I want to take a moment to look back at where this all started — and how far we’ve come together.
**Where it all started**
It all began with a simple idea: Kansans deserve a senator who actually listens to them. I never quite thought that I would run to become that senator. After all, I’m a pastor, not a politician.
But I decided to step up because I saw just how badly Washington’s chaos — and cruelty — was hurting the neighbors I love and the communities I serve.
I’ll be honest: I didn’t know exactly what to expect from a Senate race. But we hit the ground running and have come so incredibly far, all thanks to supporters like you.
**Where we are, two weeks before Election Day**
With 14 days until the big day, let me give you the lay of the land:
* The newest polls show us running neck and neck with Sen. Marshall — with some even giving us a narrow lead.
* Over the past several weeks, election experts have shifted our race further away from a “Safe Republican” rating, with RealClearPolling even calling Kansas a 50/50 TOSS-UP. _These shifts confirm that this race is going to be very close._
* The Senate Leadership Fund — a major GOP super PAC — just announced they’re launching a $15 million ad buy to attack me.

These aren’t just numbers; they are proof that Kansas is ready for change.
When I look at these metrics — which all point to this being one of the most competitive races in the nation — I am filled with gratitude for folks like you. The truth is, no one expected Kansas to become a battleground. It’s only because of this grassroots team that we’re on the brink of making history.
Whether you phone-banked or knocked on doors or chipped in a few bucks or even just shared one of these emails with a friend, you are the reason our momentum is surging.
**Please don’t forget this: All the good we do in Washington will be thanks to you. That’s something to be immensely proud of.**
**Roger Marshall’s recent months:**
Roger Marshall’s deep ties to Florida were further exposed.
“Reporting by the Kansas City Star revealed Marshall took official trips from Washington, D.C., to Sarasota, spending more than $18,000 in taxpayer funds from 2021 to 2024. The trips reportedly stopped after a hurricane destroyed the area. It is unlawful for a senator to use taxpayer money for personal travel.”
There was an embarrassing rejection by voters at the Kansas State Fair debate on his “home turf.”
It’s clear Kansans are ready for a new voice in Washington.
**It all comes down to these final two weeks.**
But right now, we find ourselves at a critical juncture. In a 50/50 toss-up race, it’s anyone’s game. It’s these last weeks that will determine who pulls ahead and whose momentum slips.
That’s why we’re gearing up, not slowing down. We’re preparing to air ads across Kansas to reach the final persuadable voters. We’re building a massive get-out-the-vote effort to ensure all of our voters have a plan to get to the ballot box.
But here is our biggest challenge: Sen. Marshall’s super PAC allies have already spent $23 million to crush our momentum, and they are gearing up to spend even more. The truth is that even our incredible momentum cannot withstand an attack this big without additional support. We need to fight back.
Here’s a little window into our campaign: Every single day, we make tough decisions on how much we can spend to reach voters based on the amount of support we receive from folks like you. **[That’s why I’m asking you to make a donation today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141845195/654955574/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk832&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNWUyODZlM2EtZWNjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=OOlp2F1EKGYFoIcpekqtGlax1DQHKbZ8QIvhxmekE7c=)**
With the stakes so incredibly high in these _make-or-break weeks_ , we truly need everyone to take an active role in this movement, in all the ways you’re able.
**So here are a few ways you can step up today:**
1. **Endorse our campaign:** Join the tens of thousands of supporters who are already all in by endorsing me for Senate. Your support is the foundation — and heart — of this movement, and **[I’d be honored to have you with me](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141845196/654955575/-1983724290?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk832&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNWUyODZlM2EtZWNjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=OOlp2F1EKGYFoIcpekqtGlax1DQHKbZ8QIvhxmekE7c=&emci=c2c283db-f0cb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=5e286e3a-eccc-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=3453560)**.
2. **Make a plan to vote:** If you're in Kansas, please make sure you have a plan to vote! Early voting has already begun and the polls are open. After all, I’m a pastor, not a politician. But I decided to step up because I saw just how badly Washington’s chaos — and cruelty — was hurting the neighbors I love and the communities I serve. State dinners are carefully staged. Every name on the guest list is a choice. When a president fills the East Room with the people who control the world’s biggest technology companies and the biggest pools of money, it isn’t an accident. It’s a message about what matters.
The evidence board

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Trump just wrapped up in NC
body:
I need your help.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1709&source=&t=1&akid=4747%2E124072%2EbKh-lw) | | | |
---
Peter,
President Trump just stepped off the stage in North Carolina after flying down for a rally in support of my GOP opponent, Michael Whatley.
He told that crowd a lot of lies – about me, my record and the grassroots movement we’re building.
And yesterday while visiting Hendersonville, JD Vance embarrassed himself _again_ when he implied “Raleigh-Durham” was the name of our capital city – you can tell he hasn't really left the airport the few times he’s been in NC!
Now, a Trump-aligned super PAC is throwing a multimillion dollar lifeline Whatley's way in a last-ditch effort to buy his way into this seat.
I know I’m getting tired of this, and I’m sure you are, too, but we can’t let up now.
Thanks to grassroots supporters like you, we’ve had the resources to fight back against the false attacks I’ve had to face thus far in the race. For that, I’m so grateful – but we’re still falling behind on the $1 million rapid-response goal my team and I set. **We’re tracking donations coming in from this email at this link:** [**_https:/ /secure.actblue.com/donate/cooper_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1709&amount=5&t=8&akid=4747%2E124072%2EbKh-lw)

clean_body: 15 days until Election Day| | | | | Patriot, it’s John James. We're just 14 days away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next Governor of Michigan. Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming election for Governor on November 3rd. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
[Barlow Logo](https://barlowforwyo.com/)

Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.

Energy = Momentum

Hi Friends,

Kelly and I continue to receive kind messages, encouragement, and prayers from folks across Wyoming. We’re grateful!

Our visits last week showcased of how much opportunity there is in Wyoming to continue extracting coal, oil, gas, uranium, and trona while innovating in manufacturing, refining, and electrical generation to supply energy and end-use products to the state, nation, and world. From refining the fuels we rely on today to building new nuclear technology, Wyoming workers and businesses have an important role in meeting our nation’s energy needs. We have the resources, experience, and people to keep leading. As governor, I’ll work to make sure those opportunities mean good jobs, strong communities, and lasting benefits for Wyoming.

I’m grateful for the recent endorsements of the Petroleum Association of Wyoming, Governor Mark Gordon, and the Wyoming Hospitality and Travel Coalition. Their support reflects the range of people and industries who want Wyoming to succeed.

Early voting is well underway, and we're hearing about many who have already headed to the polls. Let's keep it going! If you haven’t voted yet, make a plan to go this week or vote on November 3. Please reach out to three friends and encourage them to make their plans, too.

We’ll keep traveling, listening, and earning support right through Election Day. Every conversation and every vote matters. Let’s keep going through November 3.

Thank you for all you do,

Eric

October 28, 2:00 - 5:00 pm, Wyoming Taxpayers Association, Little America Hotel & Resort, 2800 W Lincolnway, Cheyenne

October 29, 8:00 - 9:00 am, Leadership at 7220, Gillette College, 300 Sinclair Street

On The Trail

LARAMIE

What a win over Northern Illinois! Go Pokes! It was great to see friends from across Wyoming at the tailgate and game, and to support First Lady Jennie Gordon’s Hunger Initiative in tackling hunger across our state.

Kelly was in Cheyenne with P.E.O. leadership and had to miss this one, but we’re looking forward to seeing everyone next week for the Cowboys and Coal game against Air Force!

KEMMEREROur visit to TerraPower in Kemmerer gave us a firsthand look at construction underway, including the test and fill facility. I joined Senator Barrasso, Governor Gordon and elected officials from Wyoming, Utah and Idaho, Department of Energy leaders, and TerraPower board and leadership to learn more about the project’s progress.Thank you to the TerraPower team for sharing their work and showing us what’s taking shape in Wyoming!

LARAMIEIt was a fun night at the 40th Annual Cowboy Joe Auction and Fundraiser! President Reeves shared Vince Lombardi’s philosophy, “Winning isn’t everything, it’s the only thing,” and the room responded with a historic evening, raising more than $1 million for athletics programs, student-athletes and the marching band. More than $75,000 was raised to support mental health programs.Thank you to Bruce and Carla Pivic for inviting me to join them for the evening. It was great to see so many folks coming together to support our Cowboys and Cowgirls!

RIVERTONWe had a great final debate in Riverton where I was happy to share my thoughts on a variety of topics.Thank you to Shanell Stanley for hosting the pre-debate Meet & Greet for myself, Kelly, and Robert Short.PHOTO CREDIT: WYOMING PBS

RIVERTON

While in Riverton for the PBS debate, Kelly and I stopped by to wish former Senate President Eli Bebout a happy birthday!

He had a ‘super’ turnout of family and friends, and I was glad to be counted among them.

LANDER

Kelly and I enjoyed our stop in Lander, including a visit to the Lander Senior Center to chat with residents, and time with students at Wyoming Catholic College.

We had a robust discussion covering life, public lands, the ESA, taxes, the role of government, energy, budgets, data centers and what government can do to help young people stay in Wyoming. When I pulled out my flip phone, the room erupted - since students aren’t allowed cell phones during the semester, it gave us all something to laugh about and bond over.

NEWCASTLE

Kelly and I appreciated spending time in Newcastle, where we toured the Weston County Children’s Center and learned more about the important work being done there to support local children and families.

We also enjoyed hosting a meet and greet at Isabella’s and spending time with folks from the community. Thank you to everyone who welcomed us and took time to visit with us during our stop in Newcastle.

NEWCASTLE

Kelly and I appreciated the opportunity to tour Wyoming Refining Company and learn more about the work being done there.

It was helpful to see the operation firsthand and hear from the team about the role the refinery plays in Wyoming’s economy and energy industry. Thank you to Brian Pischke for giving us the tour and sharing more about the work happening at the refinery.

Wyoming’s strength has always come from neighbors pitching in. Join the Barlow For Wyoming team of volunteers who are helping share his message across our state.

name: Official DNC Alert
subject: The polls are very close, Derek.
body:
The GOP is hoping that we’re all too exhausted to fight back. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 13 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=4&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=5&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu). Derek, With **fewer than _13 days_** left until Election Day, every single moment counts. We urgently need all hands on deck to reach as many voters as possible across the country to secure victories up and down the ballot for Democrats. We’ve reached out several times asking for your help to elect Democrats up and down the ballot this fall, but so far, we haven’t been able to break through. We’ve passed along messages for you from Joe Biden, Elizabeth Warren, and Hillary Clinton. We’ve explained how we’ll invest your contribution in these last **_13 days_** to help Democrats win. If you can’t afford to chip in today, we completely understand. We hope you’ll just save this email and keep in mind that your involvement and vote are essential, too. But if you can afford to make a contribution, we hope you’ll give us a chance to make one more request: **The polls are very close.** Republicans have been pouring money from their **$1 BILLION** war chest into competitive races, and they're going to keep dumping their cash until the polls close. _They’re hoping that we’re all too overwhelmed to fight back_. **We have to prove them wrong.** And the truth is that we won’t be able to reach the voters we need to contact without many more people stepping up to make their first donation of 2026. That’s why we’re reaching out to you, Derek. If everyone who receives this email donated to the DNC today, we’d blow past our October goal and have the resources we need to reach the voters we need to win. But not everyone gives, so we’re reaching out to you directly. **Democrats across America are counting on you.** [**So Derek, if you’re looking to maximize your impact in these final 13 days we’re asking you to step up right now and chip in $7 to the DNC. Time is running out, and your immediate support will send an undeniable message to Donald Trump that Democrats are coming for his majority — and _we’re going to win._ **](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261021_9990_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261021_9990_fr&t=7&akid=9990%2E22930333%2EBZQYpu)**

We’ve reached out several times asking for your help to elect Democrats up and down the ballot this fall, but so far, we haven’t been able to break through. We’ve passed along messages for you from Joe Biden, Elizabeth Warren, and Hillary Clinton. We’ve explained how we’ll invest your contribution in these last 13 days to help Democrats win. name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Indiana GOP Highlights Engling's Plan to Crack Down on Dangerous Trucking Companies
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** October 20, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Indiana GOP Highlights Engling's Plan to Crack Down on Dangerous Trucking Companies ****Indianapolis, Ind. **- The Indiana Republican Party is highlighting Secretary of State candidate Max Engling's plan to crack down on dangerous trucking companies that attempt to evade accountability by shutting down and reopening under new business names. Engling announced plans to work with the state legislature, including State Rep. Jim Pressel, to address so-called "chameleon carriers," trucking companies that use new business identities to conceal past safety violations and escape enforcement. "Changing the name on the paperwork doesn't change who is behind the wheel or who is responsible," Engling said. "If you put Hoosier families at risk, you shouldn't be able to open another LLC and pretend your record disappeared. I will work with State Representative Jim Pressel to close the gaps these operators exploit and make the Secretary of State's office an active partner in stopping business registration fraud." The plan focuses on strengthening Indiana's business registration system by identifying suspicious filings, improving coordination with law enforcement and transportation officials, and addressing gaps that allow fraudulent operators to avoid oversight."This would be a first-of-its-kind partnership in Indiana, bringing the Secretary of State's office and the legislature together to stop dangerous trucking companies from hiding behind new business names," Pressel said. "Max understands that a new LLC shouldn't erase a dangerous record. Together, we can close loopholes, protect honest truckers and make Indiana's roads safer." "Hoosiers deserve to know that dangerous trucking companies can't simply change their names and escape accountability," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "Protecting Hoosier families and supporting honest businesses should go hand in hand. Max Engling's commitment to working with the legislature to address this issue demonstrates the kind of leadership Indiana needs in its next Secretary of State." Engling's plan aims to hold bad actors accountable while protecting legitimate trucking businesses, promoting fair competition and keeping Indiana's roads safe.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhyyhjy-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. A healthcare system that guarantees every single patient can get the care they need to live and to thrive.

subject: Capitalism is a “dirty word”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vivek Ramaswamy and Rob McColley for Ohio
body:
TRUTH IS: Socialism has failed everywhere it’s been tried.

| [](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._FTag15h1SX0Ey8gpw)
---
Let me tell you something up front:
[I’m not a career politician. I don’t have all the answers – no one does. ](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
What I DO HAVE, though, is the knowledge and understanding to determine the good ideas from the bad, what doesn’t work and why. Too many young people nowadays think “capitalism” is a dirty word.
They’ve been told that it’s a system that only benefits the rich and powerful – that socialism is the way of the future. It’s what Bernie Sanders, AOC, and Zohran Mamdani preach to their followers.
But I’ll say one thing: If that’s coming from them, don’t just question it, reject it outright. It’s a calculated lie.
TRUTH IS: [Socialism has failed everywhere it’s been tried. It’s a system that stifles innovation, discourages hard work, and creates dependency on government handouts.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
We need to do better than that.
I said this recently on Fox and Friends: Capitalism is the best system known to man. It lifts people out of poverty and rewards hard work, innovation, and entrepreneurship – and it's what made America the greatest country on earth.
That shouldn’t be a taboo thought or controversial opinion.
[It’s the exact reason that the American Dream even became possible! And the reason why I'm running to be Ohio’s next Governor.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-wpf-w)
I’m proposing a bold new agenda that will make Ohio the GOLD STANDARD for every state in the Union.
We're going to:

* CAP property taxes
* ELIMINATE income tax and capital gains tax
* CUT the red tape that's strangling our economy
* Ensure Ohio LEADS the next Industrial Revolution.

This isn't just about economics – it's about values. It's about embracing success instead of apologizing for it. It's about recognizing that the American Dream is within reach for EVERYONE, no matter where they come from or who they are.
But it’ll take a team to get it done.
[So I'm humbly asking for your help: Will you join me in the fight to make Ohio America’s gold standard?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)

## Trump Unveils $8B Fuel Relief for Farmers
President Trump announced an $8 billion [Harvest Fuel Relief program](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MGupCAQBdCvwR2mKEHaBYvZuOvZztIgFC0T1A5Wa-bvJ773CW9XSSX35tw_z-npc8nb67dfyXHap42uoxAz1Sn5uqYPlUolU4qe8_bybMBPCNhLBRLV5APnkybtm-gSEVLXkFN2QGMtDLZZHHQdkkmDN8kEPUNQBiDiHD1BwBmb7O48BagUgDZ9G8LjkXSvB5sGGzEKDRQz77X9u-eNF0rl335SbcO-NsUtzO9DdL8EjgLH67raMB-34_4LHO9T4Mj1s77ljaIqF19POljePvkNlD5HgWNTXXxfuZR89FZoeK0-l68m_uFAp8P_AQAA___OdHsZ) Monday night at a rally in Park City, Kansas, to help farmers cover diesel costs during this harvest season. The one-time payments will be based on planted acres, production costs, and modeled losses for the 2026 crop year. [Crop insurance isn't required](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnTAMhq8mbEGJ4fAzMHRh-7p2RD6Jw0kVEpQYUO--SnsJ3-LhkWW_7_Pra_tCH3zcf-JBC7u0RXpKIGbKm8N8uItCpuDJWWQfd-SXwg0UDFIrCXpDw_6mrcfGLo4IqGto0eMMr3FU89h8FuOmFwzubTp8dyNaozuNc2enaVLa9V3jl3pPK9Baqf41tMZMk-uHfh7dPFqwoldkPafc_k4-8odc-JNuyq1JRxOWD_NZRPdDwCpgfZ6nvYrFdk-3gBXf6WJZgYC1lhOwnplKkZkCYaEK6n8Bq1Z1zAJWztdxSrSHj75wRvYpSowxXdFQkZN8-xAq-2C-qbCsnuR_UfLMac94NHmx51P3yjCKXu0H-vAvMn_T9L3A3wAAAP__qsiUHQ), and payment rates for major crops are due in November. Diesel [averaged about $6.31](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHO3CAQBOCnwR0WYM7YBUUad3_alNYaL_YmGE6wd7_u7SPnFdKPPs3Mr6_1CyhRPn7ChZ5jWTN-t4TMWNcI9YovTBUTYdyBKR_ADwWrUWaUWkmjVwhMb1wtdLuPiAaHDr12s3k4p2bXnR7DFm0IgLANOM2bHo0ejJtctMHCiB3529PKaK2UfYx9CNMU7WhnF2e3m11YhTtxqf3vQplPjOlT3lj7UK4u-ZP52cTwQ5hFmCVShhyw_8BZyp0QZrmg_kFuwixQmUJCYRaur-spIefyygGbnORGKVHJMpYq7-1Ym-QiS4wNWbYClfIhd8KGSYbSuEmt9TCoaVb9yVfqqt-f37fSRiesOi6g9K8k_-e3b2_-BgAA__9ap5Bj) a gallon Monday, after hitting a record high in September as conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine tightened global supply. President Trump credited Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., with [pushing the program through](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHSnCAUBeCn0Q4H-FGWgiKN3aZN6Vzh4pIgOHBds2-fMa_w92e-Oef8ei5PiCnm7SfsaCmUJePVEhJhXQLUPZyYKqaIwQPFvAGNHBbJ5cQEZ1Is4Ci-cVHQexsQJX71aIU2ctSaG92_rNAc9Do6YyZjxqCEd5NXxkvupwDO9NHenuBSCM7VOA3OPR5BTcroYLSXvlMcfaRSh98lZnphSJ_yxjq4svfJvoiO1n396OTcyfm6riGUv-vZYsbW7kwnZ8xYt08nZ6rnfjDIuZzZYWOPla0QUzmJ3XuxNuZum_mIDRNzpRFrZ92QwR49AyJwfxrbUlkhsXYeR_r01frjiinFNulO8W2HmP63o2-e-rbyXwAAAP__v7yPrw) and said fuel prices would plunge once the Iran war ends, promising more farm funding if Republicans win next month.
## Offshore Nor'easter Floods East Coast Beaches
A strengthening nor'easter hundreds of miles out in the Atlantic is bringing [days of onshore winds](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUDGO7CAUOw3pEsEbApOC4jfp5rdbRgQeCSsCI_Jm0N5-lbnCNpZsS7bsr8fysDHFvP23BxoKZcnYzoREWJdg6xFemCqmiMFbinmzNHK7AAfVC96DWKyj-MZF2s6bgAh469AIPcGoNZ90txvp9epXJcOKegQJGpUIo3cI_CbusHbRXHmCgxCcy1ENzt3vQSo56TBpD55Jjj5SqcN3iZl2DOmnvLEOrhxdMjvR82S3fwxmBnNrbciru3Zc_qWgpR0rg_mkUo-TwfwsDWt4pR7tSVh7t79qjnn78N6VC6vLVnE5StlV458tphRPpZnk22Fj-pTTHz97G_gNAAD__0LfgdM) and coastal flooding from the Jersey Shore to the Outer Banks, with flood advisories posted for 1 to 2 feet of inundation. ## Frozen Kidneys Open Transplant Options
University of Minnesota researchers froze whole pig kidneys into a glass-like state at [minus 238 degrees Fahrenheit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO2zAQAF8jdWuQa0k0CxVp3F3alMJCXMp7oUiDXMnwvT64fOHqAQaD-fOxfJAkydtv2nnWWJbMr5ZYlesSqe7x4FQ5CcdAKnkjHQ0taHACawDtQqvKyctAfZgjM_K159k6j6Nzxrv-MTOis8PobJzQU6TJoPfuyjxYj8GMvczfPmvQWmOGcbqs6-0Wh2nwLnoXMHSD4SBa6uWzSNYHx_QuJ9fLWvY-zQ_VZ-uuvzq8d3jf5GsvoXyzDu9tFc4qTRt8Hk2h8iknB3jKBn8lZH43iLV8cYZYKhC8mSqIwlqOFKDyq4oy6IMhHnpUhhKh1I0yaKXcnomyNkBjzA2ddb6vc3i-JCVpk-sGs-0k6X-o_vDvOeO_AAAA__-PAJFZ), stored them for more than a year, and brought them back to working order. The breakthrough could have major implications for organ donation. Donor kidneys currently last only 24 to 36 hours on ice, and about [20% of donated kidneys](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ9GOwz8q6IFxTXb7bVXGgKDcodoAN349hfvFa6aTDKZzHxfr-mlffBx_tQrVHHbFPHOAaUgTU6n1R0ICcHDWV18nHXpuJ6IU88EZyQmbYo_MbW6tsoBhEcNJeRInZR8lPWiBMlheIiBAGlsR4NxpPVoaLS96Ye29uruE5yE4Lzt-saYYXBt347SjdKSrVoO68uWmu_Nx7LAhWs7kRqzrXVQSyl7rh4fFT0repqM5lhjA3vcbgsBMyp63sduyY65I1pYlpChk1mQMsuHMcjZHSFcrCQd8x50LMyka9vvYDph2e5n9uNtxFUnZfe3D8HnXlYtn1ftw9-e8k-Mp6LfAAAA__971oov) go unused because they can’t reach a recipient in time. More than 100,000 Americans are on the transplant waiting list. To freeze them, the organs were loaded with chemical antifreeze and iron oxide nanoparticles, then rewarmed evenly with an electromagnetic field. After thawing, the kidneys [regained their color](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMpDdGAyBg03IZtMNUa_dhl4ZPLI9g2ZP_8W_wk-rpCq99-exPpAjn9tvPMjWkNaTrhKpVsprwHyEF8VMkSl4rHxuWAeJK0gYWyVbUCu6ym9aNTbeBiKgviGrzAyDMXI2zW6N7KdBG-c1eByCmsmPfzGYEQzNasaG7b2nJCglpR7GzrlpCnrUswmz8eCFluS5ptz9S3zWnUL8pDflzqWjiXav9VlE_0vAImC5rqv74J7S3QpYbiABS3FMpyMBC-bKLtIdbhFLaUNO_-lsDz5fpYV-akOrtBqkHI3u9nrEJlv_vDhGLqMRWm4Hcvw-rz909rbwFQAA____4X9s) and produced urine within about a minute of transplant. The thawed kidneys produced only about two-thirds the normal amount of urine, and the results [await peer review](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAUgOHT4C3o8QIGBoYu3tK1o4Xh4VBhExFqt7ev0iv0Av8n_R-3-eZzyfv67jdyPdV5p_NZqHdqc_JtS19UGpVMKfqe99V3BX5GwPEi4IJi9qHng2bph-gSEdJ1ICe0RaU1WD3cXTQipKRVWkQYjfRqMaSVWKw0SiDIIbtXTwAKASDVyEMwJslRWp2sjhiZBIq518Y_a977nVL5qQc1Huo2FHfv_fFk1zeGE8PpPE--5Nq-88FrWxlOoe6d9s5wEsBHaaxhOL1ILoCD5lqN1sIhhubi48yl5OeomYR187n8Gf2faw6HvwEAAP__kDlzzw). name: Josh Shapiro
subject: I know it’s early. But I need you to read this.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA
body:
It still might not be enough

Derek, I know it’s the crack of dawn. But I need you to read this: We are thirteen days out from Election Day. We’ve got organizers on the ground across Pennsylvania. We’ve got TV ads running in every media market across Pennsylvania. **And it still might not be enough.** That’s the thing about Pennsylvania. It doesn’t matter if you’re thirteen days out, thirteen hours out, or even thirteen minutes out. Thousands of voters will make their final decision the moment they start filling out their ballot on November 3rd. So if we slow down for even a second? Friend,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

MIDWEEK MEMO

Patriots~

Greetings this beautiful fall season. I love this time of year for many personal reasons, however, I also enjoy this season for a
professional reason too. Five years ago this week I began serving as the Republican Party of Minnesota's Deputy Chair. First
appointed by the newly elected chair in a special election in October of 2021, then subsequently elected three additional times.
Serving as your Deputy Chair has been a highlight of my lifetime. I am immensely grateful to everyone who has shouldered any part
of Party operations during this time.

In fact, the most endearing aspect of Party operations, in my humble opinion, is working alongside the amazing volunteers that
show up to do the work, make the calls, knock the doors and help raise those much-needed political contributions. I have often
said — and firmly believe — that our Party runs on our volunteers. My gratitude for each and every one of you.

I have traveled this state for many a fundraiser, parade, rally, event, and more, and strived to work in the Edina Party office at
least once a week. Just from my home in Duluth to the Edina Party office is 170 mi one way. That driving time allowed for many
phone calls and for listening to podcasts or political talk shows that have provided inspiration, talking points and new ideas.
Strategies and solutions were often times crafted during those drives.

MAKE A PLAN TO VOTE NOW

If there is one take-away from this position that I know to be completely true it is this: If you don't cast your ballot the
entire Republican team loses an important vote. In both 2022 and 2024, Party operations calculated thousands of good Republicans
who were needed to cast a ballot, and did not. Despite best intentions, some people missed voting at the polls on election day due
to one reason or another. I urge you to not let that happen this year.

In fact, I was recently at an event where I asked everyone in the audience to "pinky swear" with me that they promise to crawl
through broken glass to get to the polling stations and cast their ballots if they are going to wait to vote on November 3rd. (OK,
maybe figuratively, but you get my point). Kids get sick, cars break down, and weather happens. I urge you to make a plan to vote
NOW. If you are in a mail in only precinct, send that ballot in asap. This election is an all-hands-on-deck moment. We cannot win
if we don't vote.

## Texas Early Voting Draws Record Crowds

body:

**Peter, things aren't looking good:**
1\. President Trump personally attacked me when he came to North Carolina to campaign for my opponent, saying I’d make North Carolina a "killing field."
2\. Far-right super PACs – including a Trump-aligned group – have spent tens of millions to defeat me and prop up my Republican opponent, Michael Whatley.
3\. Their attacks are working: Our momentum is slipping. **That’s why Trump came back to North Carolina _yesterday_ to double down on these attacks, and why a GOP super PAC just announced _another_ million-dollar attack ad buy._**
**Trump, Vance and the entire MAGA machine are coming after me as a top target – because if we lose here, Democrats will lose our shot at flipping the Senate.[_I need your immediate grassroots support to fight back, so please, can I count on you to chip in today?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1700&amount=5&t=9&akid=4654%2E124072%2EjuiG_o)**

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

name: James Carville
subject: New Hampshire is a coin flip (MEMO)
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
One poll has Sununu ahead. One has Pappas ahead. One has it tied. Here's what that means for the Senate majority.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261021_1.e9KxcC&refcode=em20261021-1&t=1&akid=9658%2E582294%2Ez3HbDq)
Hi. It's James Carville.
I've been sounding the alarm about New Hampshire for months. I said Chris Pappas’s race was being ignored. I said the math didn't work without it. I said John Sununu was a uniquely dangerous opponent.
Now we’ve got just days to go, and the polls are all over the map. One has Sununu ahead. One has it dead even. One has Pappas up. That tells me one thing: **This race is anyone's game.**
I put together an urgent memo to explain what that means. Read it right now. Then help Chris Pappas win this thing.
**[If you don't need convincing, rush a $5 donation to Chris Pappas's campaign immediately.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261021_1.e9KxcC&refcode=em20261021-1&t=2&akid=9658%2E582294%2Ez3HbDq)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261021_1.e9KxcC&amount=5&refcode=em20261021-1&t=3&akid=9658%2E582294%2Ez3HbDq)**
* * *
* * *
**OCTOBER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON NH-SEN**
**FROM:** James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
**TO:** Interested Parties
I need to be clear with you about where things stand in the race for New Hampshire's open Senate seat. This race is a coin flip, and it is going to stay that way until the very last vote is cast.
**_The polls are a mixed bag, and that should worry every Democrat._**
* The University of New Hampshire's Granite State Poll had **John Sununu ahead of Chris Pappas in August, 45% to 43%.**
* And in September, it was a total mixed bag:
* Republicans' own polling for the National Republican Senatorial Committee had Sununu up by a point, 37% to 36%.
* A co/efficient poll had the race **tied** at 46% apiece.
* The _New York Times_ /Siena poll had Pappas up 50% to 45%.
* Put those together, and you don't get a frontrunner. You get a race that could go either way, and Republicans know it.

**_The GOP's investment in this race keeps growing._**
* Some $60 million+ in outside money has already flooded New Hampshire to boost Sununu and attack Pappas. That's in a state with fewer than one million registered voters. Voters are getting absolutely hammered with Republican ads.
* The Senate Leadership Fund has announced $17 million for Sununu.
* A Trump-aligned super PAC has reserved another $10 million in New Hampshire ads.
* Koch-backed Americans for Prosperity Action has already spent over $15 million.
* John Sununu is not a back-bench candidate. He has a famous New Hampshire political name (his father and his brother both served as governor), he has won a statewide election here before, and he has the full weight of the Republican donor machine behind him.
* **Republicans understand the math perfectly.** They don't need to flip five seats like we do. They just need to flip New Hampshire red and make Democrats' path to a majority impossible.

**_In New Hampshire almost nobody has voted yet._**
* In states around the country, voters are already casting their ballots. New Hampshire is different.
* There's no early in-person voting here, and absentee voting requires an excuse. Roughly nine in ten Granite Staters cast their ballots in person on Election Day itself.
* New Hampshire also has same-day voter registration. In 2024 nearly 93,000 people registered at the polls on Election Day.
* **_That means this race is not even close to decided._** Nearly every vote that will decide it is still out there, and every one of them is still up for grabs. We have to stay vigilant.

**_New Hampshire has decided control before — and the margins are razor thin._**
* In 2016 the New Hampshire Senate race was decided by just 1,017 votes.
* When Democrats chart a path to retaking the Senate majority, New Hampshire is not optional. If Chris Pappas loses, Democrats need to flip five seats instead of four. That math does not exist.

**_Races like this are won in the final weeks._**
* I have worked Senate races in every corner of this country. And I can tell you from hard experience: When a race is this close, it gets decided by the side that shows up in the final stretch with the resources to finish strong.
* In New Hampshire the final stretch is everything. When nearly the whole electorate votes on one day, the last ad they see and the last door that gets knocked matter more than anywhere else in the country.
* I am telling you right now: Chris Pappas can win this race. But only if we give him what he needs to compete between now and November 3rd.

**_Chris Pappas has what it takes to win — but he needs resources right now._**
* Pappas has won New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District four times without a loss. He just won his primary with 65% of the vote. He knows how to reach voters across the aisle and build a coalition that wins.
* Pappas has outraised Sununu candidate-to-candidate, thanks to support from hundreds of thousands of individual donors. **_But that advantage gets swallowed up fast when over $60 million in outside money is hitting the airwaves._**
* In a race that could come down to a few thousand votes, being drowned out on TV in the final weeks is the ballgame. We are in that moment right now.

* * *
* * *
Listen. I don't write memos like this for every race, and I don't send urgent updates unless I'm genuinely worried.
_I'm telling you: I'm worried about New Hampshire._
The polls are split. Republicans are spending like crazy. And almost every vote in this race is still waiting to be cast.
**[Rush a donation to Chris Pappas immediately. Don't let New Hampshire be the race we wish we'd done more for when we had the chance.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261021_1.e9KxcC&refcode=em20261021-1&t=4&akid=9658%2E582294%2Ez3HbDq)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261021_1.e9KxcC&amount=5&refcode=em20261021-1&t=23&akid=9658%2E582294%2Ez3HbDq)**
Right now is our time to play ball. Let's elect Chris Pappas and flip the Senate.
– James Carville
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**

I always tell my supporters, “If you are going to have my sign in your yard, you need to be a good neighbor. _And_ if someone on your street has a Roger Marshall sign up, be kind to them, too. Say, ‘Hey, I know we disagree, but that’s OK. I love you as my neighbor just the same.’"

I know there are a lot of problems that are making life harder right now. Cuts to healthcare, skyrocketing gas prices, out-of-control grocery costs ... the list goes on and on.

**When I’m elected, I’ll fight to fix those problems for every single person, regardless of whether they voted for me or Roger Marshall. clean_body: We can disagree and still love each other. | | | = Friend, I was in a crowded coffee shop in Topeka a few weeks ago listening to Kansans talk about their challenges, dreams and hopes for the future. While I was there, I shared the most fundamental message of my campaign: Remember to be a good neighbor. You don’t have to agree with someone to love them. In fact, our system works best when we disagree, because then we can find a compromise that addresses the concerns of both sides. I know this may not be a typical approach to politics, but the only way to solve the problems our country is facing is to find a way to work together — even when we disagree. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Friend, I’m not a career politician. In Washington, I’ll fight against the chaos and division, but that starts right here in Kansas. I always tell my supporters, “If you are going to have my sign in your yard, you need to be a good neighbor. And if someone on your street has a Roger Marshall sign up, be kind to them, too. Say, ‘Hey, I know we disagree, but that’s OK. I love you as my neighbor just the same.’" I know there are a lot of problems that are making life harder right now. Cuts to healthcare, skyrocketing gas prices, out-of-control grocery costs ... the list goes on and on. When I’m elected, I’ll fight to fix those problems for every single person, regardless of whether they voted for me or Roger Marshall. But nothing we do to fix what’s broken will matter if we can’t be good neighbors. If we can’t find a way to love each other through our differences. I am excited to announce that Hillsdale's online teaching series, ["Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer,"](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckU-L2zAQxT-NfLORRvKfPfiw4KQsNFtKDj0KRRo7A5IlLDlLv30xTfMBepw3j_dj5v266IshT-vyaQKOlLN20WlH2cYHbvf4hTauMZDNFJKxGjh0teA1CG1soQdqZSo3tiCGeahwFP0btIMCAdV95D03M9h2uOGbtfw2iLlrzdwrKeSshKpoPPIEByGAS3hrenFzyt46GAxXggNTfE_OFGxozeQw2xhTip4K2dzEban8eC8lZSbfGZwZnDPafUPX3Mn77IzHBt3O4PyaD8-ekv9dH4H16776UONWavdwTJ6zZXLiHEB8clDwXbTTj-l0ujLo9hJ0jvtmkckpbTEntIXW5bkK6GgPTE4YDPmnaE1IhpaVyekvXR90_aLrg_q0xrXgWpicPi7v3076Z19_XK_1v09V2-jSF3lPueuZ4stBaWwMVfnf_h4j_AkAAP__szetbg) is now available to own as a DVD box set.

In this series, you will discover how taxation, regulation, money, government spending, and trade influence our decisions and impact our lives. Joined by Steve Forbes, Stephen Moore, Larry Kudlow, Amity Shlaes, Brian Domitrovic, and Larry P. Arnn, Dr. Laffer explains how supply-side economics holds the key to unleashing American prosperity once again.

But we need the support of citizens like you to promote this series to millions of Americans along with our other nationwide outreach.

Will you partner with us to promote this free online teaching series from Hillsdale College and expand other educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty? Your tax-deductible donation will help us to enroll thousands of Americans in this series.

And for a donation of $100 or more, we will send you this beautiful DVD box set of "Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer."

**To help support this course and get your copy of "Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer" on DVD, click the link below:**

[https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/supply-side-economics-support-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckU-L2zAQxT-NfLORRvKfPfiw4KQsNFtKDj0KRRo7A5IlLDlLv30xTfMBepw3j_dj5v266IshT-vyaQKOlLN20WlH2cYHbvf4hTauMZDNFJKxGjh0teA1CG1soQdqZSo3tiCGeahwFP0btIMCAdV95D03M9h2uOGbtfw2iLlrzdwrKeSshKpoPPIEByGAS3hrenFzyt46GAxXggNTfE_OFGxozeQw2xhTip4K2dzEban8eC8lZSbfGZwZnDPafUPX3Mn77IzHBt3O4PyaD8-ekv9dH4H16776UONWavdwTJ6zZXLiHEB8clDwXbTTj-l0ujLo9hJ0jvtmkckpbTEntIXW5bkK6GgPTE4YDPmnaE1IhpaVyekvXR90_aLrg_q0xrXgWpicPi7v3076Z19_XK_1v09V2-jSF3lPueuZ4stBaWwMVfnf_h4j_AkAAP__szetbg)

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

Peter, in case you missed it: **Donald Trump wants to change the name of New Mexico to New America.** [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16858?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.21_Haaland-New-America_B1_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=5&akid=3616%2E259176%2EaEijWB) Instead of focusing on the issues that matter to hardworking families, he’s pushing another distraction while families face higher costs and rising gas prices.

Being New Mexican is something special.

Our roots run deep. They’re in the acequias, cornfields, lowriders, and chile harvests. In the food we cook and the traditions we pass down, and in the communities that have cared for one another for generations.

My roots here run 35 generations deep. I am the proud descendant of fierce Pueblo women, a grandfather who worked as a diesel mechanic and tended his cornfield, a grandmother who taught me to love New Mexican cooking, and parents who taught me the meaning of service and sacrifice.

These aren’t just my stories. **_They’re part of what makes New Mexico, New Mexico._**

So when Donald Trump talks about taking away the name and identity that generations of New Mexicans have built, I can’t just stand by. And when my opponent wants to bring Donald Trump’s agenda to New Mexico and cut Medicaid, SNAP, and Universal Childcare, I have to fight back.

I have a vision for New Mexico that starts with our people: **higher wages, lower costs, stronger schools, and healthcare that’s there when you need it.** I want to invest in mental and behavioral healthcare, substance use treatment, rehabilitation, and housing stability so we can build safer, stronger communities.
**_But I can’t do it alone._** [**That’s why I need your help right now. I have run for office at some of the most pivotal and dramatic moments of the last decade — narrowly losing a House seat in 2017 (the first big special election after Trump was elected) and winning one of the two historic Senate runoffs in 2021...

# [Do data centers really drain America's water?](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=220243597&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwMjQzNTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTI1OTEwMTYsImV4cCI6MTc5NTE4MzAxNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.bqHRMauT5FSNhdh0rz7uOKwKmMeRfRk4NvSBJVJs3BQ)
### The fight over data centers is one of America's newest--and fiercest--political battlefields.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Oct 21
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=220243597&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwMjQzNTk3LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc5MjU5MTAxNiwiZXhwIjoxNzk1MTgzMDE2LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMjQ0MDM5OCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.LmEw1ufKfDGqCG8z9pctWEr15nIC6LI6321zn2fkax0&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

| | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/do-data-centers-really-drain-americas-water?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwMjQzNTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTI1OTEwMTYsImV4cCI6MTc5NTE4MzAxNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.bqHRMauT5FSNhdh0rz7uOKwKmMeRfRk4NvSBJVJs3BQ&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/do-data-centers-really-drain-americas-water?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store-no-desktop&inbox=true&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

One of the most remarkable shifts in U.S. politics since the 2024 elections--coincident with the rise of AI--is the emergence of a hardened, overwhelming, and bipartisan aversion to data centers.
We're currently in the "endlessly inundated with ads" phase of the '26 midterm elections, and everyone seems to be leaning into the attack that their opponent is pro-data center. [Republicans are using it to attack Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/74a681b9-2812-4577-bb65-786f377f74e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); [Democrats are using it to attack Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/6a305c61-808f-4c2a-a3fb-b76069305371?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [sometimes in the same race](https://substack.com/redirect/8e791651-83c3-4e26-8452-26dd9458419c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg);1 [ballot measure campaigns are using the tactic](https://substack.com/redirect/31140f36-1416-4850-aebf-1071ffea2eba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to win over voters even when their campaign has literally nothing to do with data centers.2
[Within a matter of months](https://substack.com/redirect/72402789-078f-4bac-a441-a28c0c5a03fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), support for building data centers has crumbled.
At the same time, setting aside the narrative, what I haven't seen: what's the real story with data centers? Where is public opinion on the mark, and where is public anger unjustified?3
I'm splitting this discussion across two articles. In this one, I'll talk about public opinion, what's driving those opinions, and the top reason Americans are concerned about data centers: their water use.
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _The water that data centers use is a minuscule percentage of the country 's total water use: less than 1%, even broadly defined. But that undersells the impact they're having._
> * _During the summer, in arid places, and in places without adequate regulation, the water data centers are using is a legitimate and growing problem._
> * _States and municipalities must update their laws to require more efficient technology and to charge more for data centers to use and consume water._
>

[ Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjIwMjQzNTk3LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzkyNTkxMDE2LCJleHAiOjIxMDgxNjcwMTYsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.wVincWlrU2VNsXPcUoC9PblG1a_2Wojvc2444ng-Kzs?)
## Americans are concerned about data centers
Ordinarily, I'm perfectly comfortable using polling data from a year or two ago--certainly, from a few months ago--because while public opinion shifts on issues, it's usually pretty slow.
That's not the case with data centers. In a matter of months, public opinion on data centers has become [considerably more negative](https://substack.com/redirect/72402789-078f-4bac-a441-a28c0c5a03fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a change across every demographic and across both Republicans and Democrats.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/464b52d9-fccf-4d07-93df-cadd6cbecaa9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Ipsos](https://substack.com/redirect/60164793-ddc3-4653-b3d1-d15207a43884?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), September 9-10
For context, that's [higher than the percentage of Americans who are concerned](https://substack.com/redirect/5f84bdea-28a9-456b-a577-39471e788c15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about future terrorist attacks, crime, and unemployment.4 This is a real concern for people.
In the same poll, people who were concerned about the growth of data centers were asked why specifically they were concerned:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6279c51-c92f-4f03-b48b-b5e6ba631a05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Ipsos](https://substack.com/redirect/60164793-ddc3-4653-b3d1-d15207a43884?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), September 9-10
I'll use this data as a way of defining people's top six concerns with data centers.5 With data centers having become such a toxic political issue, I wanted to understand: **how real are these issues?** Where's the narrative about data centers right, and where is it wrong?
In this article, I'm focusing just on the top concern that Americans have: how much water data centers use. In the next one, I'll focus on the next five issues that worry us.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=220243597&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwMjQzNTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTI1OTEwMTYsImV4cCI6MTc5NTE4MzAxNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.bqHRMauT5FSNhdh0rz7uOKwKmMeRfRk4NvSBJVJs3BQ)
## 1\. Are data centers a strain on local water supplies?
Right now, the water that data centers use is a really, really small percentage of total water use in the United States. Data centers use about [38.5 billion gallons of water](https://substack.com/redirect/d18d66a7-f6d6-4949-b984-ee78392b3640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) per year. The country as a whole uses [102.6 ](https://substack.com/redirect/3eb3b64b-5377-4440-9a51-5ba85cab67c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/3eb3b64b-5377-4440-9a51-5ba85cab67c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ --that's 102,600 billion--gallons of freshwater per year.6 **Data centers make up about 0.04% of the country 's total water use.**
On the one hand, that's nothing.7 On the other, it almost certainly undersells how much water data centers consume, and undersells the impact that data centers have on water supplies in the U.S.
Even still, for most of the United States, we're a long way from water use becoming a substantial strain on our systems. But there are places where it is a real issue.
#### Water use ≠ water withdrawals ≠ water consumption
Before we dig into any of the data, there are some definitions that matter.
Water use is any water that we use: for households, for agriculture, for power, etc. Water withdrawals refer to any water removed from rivers, lakes, groundwater, etc. And water consumption is any water that isn't returned to the immediate water environment, usually because it's lost to evaporation or because it's incorporated into products.8
I give you (and myself) this lesson in ecology because how much water is _used_ generally matters less than how much water is _consumed_. It turns out that data centers are quite consumptive:
* [According to Google disclosures](https://substack.com/redirect/20d8f653-940e-43f0-a8fd-46c7bf8cd481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 78% of the water they use at their data centers is consumed.
* [According to Meta disclosures](https://substack.com/redirect/453bdcc3-f8d3-496c-984d-db51393faef5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 72% of the water they use at their data centers is consumed.

This is very high! It's on par with irrigation, where [72% of water use is consumptive](https://substack.com/redirect/5dd8f139-a319-4eed-b15f-df786b0d7eb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There are two points I'd add here for important context.
First, [tech](https://substack.com/redirect/0a3f5dd8-1c63-4b08-b9fb-3aa10c72b912?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [companies](https://substack.com/redirect/4ad9716e-d462-4adc-856e-77c4e7f741dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [are](https://substack.com/redirect/a19b9a45-bb51-4de6-a896-194c525bb5d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [promising](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8fb654-d6c6-419b-92b8-2edba9cb11bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more efficient water use at their data centers, and while they have some incentive to overpromise here, their incentives are generally aligned--saving water generally saves money--and I suspect this technology will get better over time.
Second, while the data centers themselves may be highly consumptive, power production generally isn't. For power production, [only about 4% of water use](https://substack.com/redirect/afe0a178-d0df-4b0a-b178-a1f08169bbbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is consumptive, though that varies considerably based on the mode of power generation.9
#### That 0.04% estimate doesn't include power generation
With that said, we should talk about the water that's being used to generate the power that runs data centers.
Saying that data centers account for 0.04% of the country's water use accounts only for direct water use, i.e., water used by the equipment on-site at data centers. But that discounts the water consumed by having to generate more energy--and [that indirect water consumption is estimated to be as much as 12× more](https://substack.com/redirect/98f99181-0869-4a0e-9129-5352c191d15a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than any direct water consumption.10
Again, this varies a lot based on how the energy is being generated. But incremental power generation substantially increases the impact on water systems that data centers can have.
#### Water use is highly seasonal
[Water use is not constant](https://substack.com/redirect/a49f9baa-cfdd-4daf-bb3b-a0573e090910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) throughout the year. Namely, in most of the United States, [water use is higher](https://substack.com/redirect/d11ed264-3537-4947-ae78-5361e60bf4a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during the summer.11
That's true at data centers too. Because it's warmer and [more water is needed for cooling](https://substack.com/redirect/0d02d196-c2cb-4c26-8db8-0fe61419c257?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), monthly water use at data centers is often [much higher during the summer than the rest of the year](https://substack.com/redirect/16baec17-3599-4b27-9658-686c0023acc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That coincides with periods--namely, the late summer and early fall--when American water levels are [generally at their lowest](https://substack.com/redirect/0d37998b-5333-4638-8864-163b7bfbdaab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
So even if data centers use a low percentage of a region's water on average, they can still seasonally strain water systems because of when their water usage is highest.
#### Water usage varies greatly across the United States
Something else we all know: the [amount of water available](https://substack.com/redirect/deeb8b48-bb9a-4389-b8cb-7b3b81821224?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--and the [amount of water used](https://substack.com/redirect/7da27bdb-9a81-4f81-94d5-6dca23296796?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--varies drastically by state. Arizona, for instance, has the [seventh-most data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/6d01e28c-f832-4428-8fd3-7171b2ed23e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the United States, at a time when its water availability is already under incredible strain because of a [sustained drought impacting the Colorado River](https://substack.com/redirect/5830b425-b2d7-49c4-9bd7-230e907076f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In [Arizona and elsewhere in the Mountain West](https://substack.com/redirect/836e1608-40bd-445f-8c1e-94d267dab58b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), where this is an issue, data centers are a particular threat. That's less true in other places where water availability is less of a pressing issue.
#### Left unregulated, data centers really can wreak havoc on local water
Back in 2006, Google opened a data center in [The Dalles, Oregon](https://substack.com/redirect/9f98607b-0838-4e06-8f10-dab5fe4b0803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a city with 16,000 people about 90 minutes east of Portland. Google has since opened several more there, and its [data centers use about 33% of the city's water supply](https://substack.com/redirect/d0bb545a-1d27-491e-b31a-8dab452cdf87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).12
This creates all sorts of issues for the city (and for wildlife in the region).
In Louisiana, [Meta is building a data center](https://substack.com/redirect/195a54e3-3556-4b30-9acc-a6a677fbd8b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in [Richland Parish](https://substack.com/redirect/0a3fb7c0-2e58-4589-a4ac-a43fb56a9573?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).13 When it opens in 2028, its daily water usage is projected to be comparable to the [daily water usage for 17,000 people](https://substack.com/redirect/9a81bbd3-2c83-4298-8e2d-5a8bbdc7d6e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the parish, which is notable because only 20,000 people live there.14
There are plenty of examples like this from across America.
#### What's incorrect about the narrative about water use at data centers?
I already talked about the big thing: today, data centers are still using a tiny percentage of American water. For most of the country, it'd be wrong to say that this is a pressing, imminent threat.
If we were serious about addressing water use in the United States, [we'd start with agriculture](https://substack.com/redirect/45d5fd1f-6056-4455-980a-348a204a1e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), not data centers. [Agriculture is pretty horribly inefficient](https://substack.com/redirect/e7339b6f-d695-434c-a635-d00f214d287f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and consumes substantially more water than data centers will anytime soon.
Yes, agriculture is also more essential. But small reductions in agricultural water consumption would outweigh even substantial improvements in the efficiency of water use at data centers.
But that doesn't mean that data centers shouldn't be doing much more--especially since they're poised to continue expanding at such a rapid pace.
**Verdict: the water that data centers use is a tiny percentage of America 's total water use. Data centers don't necessarily threaten the water supply in all of America, since they're so localized. But if you live in an area with data centers, or if you live in an arid area, they can--and do--have a real and lasting impact on water systems.**
